newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends weaker on Plains weather forecasts.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends weaker on Plains weather forecasts.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures settled lower on forecasts for generally dry weather in the southern Plains, which traders said should allow harvest to resume in full force.

"The weather looks such that harvest will get going at a steady clip over the next five to seven days," a KCBT trader said. "Our weather people have also seen a good chance for rain in North Dakota by the end of the weekend."
Traders said volumes were sluggish as players kept to the sidelines ahead of the Thursday release of USDA's June Supply/Demand and winter wheat production reports.
"Tomorrow's report has kept activity at a minimum," the trader said.
Losses were limited by spillover strength from MGE spring wheat, which was buoyed by dryness in North Dakota.
KCBT wheat settled steady to 2-1/2 cents per bushel lower, with July down 1-1/4 cents at $3.87-1/2.
Traders said commercial firm Continental Grain and commission house Refco each bought at least one million July bushels. Benson-Quinn sold 1.5 million July.
